title: Differential spatial distribution of EGCG@ZIF-8 within nanofibers enables programmed release for infected wound healing
content: Pathological scars are often visible in damaged tissues. Under the inflammatory state, oxidative toxins and bacteria interfere with the regeneration process, damage the wound, and thus form scars. To accurately intervene in each stage of infected wound treatment, a PG/E@Z dressing was developed. The dressing contains polycaprolactone/gelatin composite nanofibers composed of (−)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG)-loaded zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8). EGCG and Zn2+ form nanoparticles (NPs) through polyphenol–metal coordination and are integrated into the bionic nanofiber network. The differential spatial distribution of E@Z nanoparticles within the nanofibers allows for programmed release. By modulating the exposure levels of nanoparticles, the rapid release of EGCG and Zn2+ is achieved in the early stage in order to exert an antibacterial effect. This is followed by the sustained release of bioactive components in the later stage in order to alleviate oxidative stress and promote tissue remodelling. Due to the synergistic effect of EGCG and Zn2+, PG/E@Z shows broad antibacterial properties, strong reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging ability, excellent cell compatibility, and can accelerate the fibroblast migration. An in vivo methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)-infected wound model further confirmed that PG/E@Z markedly enhances wound closure, collagen deposition, and reduces inflammatory cell infiltration, while attenuating scar formation. PG/E@Z reduces myofibroblast differentiation and scar formation by removing excess ROS, blocking the TGF-β/Smad3 fibrosis pathway, and decreasing the nuclear translocation of p-Smad3 and reducing α-SMA expression. This article presents a promising strategy for multistage infected wound management by employing a nanofiber dressing with integrated structural and functional design.
